Class 2 · Chapter 5 of 9

Length, weight, capacity and temperature

Measure from zero, compare weight and capacity, and read a thermometer.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Lines, shapes and solids. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can measure and compare lengths.
  • I can compare weight and capacity.
  • I can compare thermometer readings.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Start measuring at zero

Line up the start of the pencil with 0 on the ruler.

Read the number at the other end. This pencil is 7 cm long.

Screen 2 of 4

Heavier and lighter

A balance tips down on the heavier side.

Here the right side is heavier. If both sides match, they weigh the same.

Screen 3 of 4

How much fits?

Capacity tells how much a jug holds.

Jug B holds 5 cups. Jug A holds 3 cups. Jug B holds 2 cups more.

Screen 4 of 4

Read a thermometer

A thermometer scale works like a number line.

Higher up means hotter. 30 degrees is warmer than 25 degrees.

Words to know
length
How long something is, measured in cm or m.
weight
How heavy something is, measured in g or kg.
capacity
How much a container holds, measured in mL or litres.
temperature
How hot or cold something is, in degrees.

For parents

What your child learns

When we measure with blocks, each block is one unit, such as 1 cm. A heavier pan tips down on a balance. We can find how many full portions fit by dividing what is left.

A common slip

Children often start measuring from the end of a ruler, not from zero, or ignore a remainder. Line up the start at 0. In division, only full portions count.

5-minute home activity: Measure and weigh

  1. Measure a spoon or pencil with a ruler from 0.
  2. Compare three objects by holding one in each hand.
  3. Rank them from lightest to heaviest.
  4. Cut a paper strip into 5 cm pieces and count the whole ones.
